newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE options active as UK shares jump.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE options active as UK shares jump.

text.p: A positive tone to the London stock market and the expiry of May stock options combined to swell UK equity traded options volumes on Wednesday, dealers said.
The greater liquidity and prospects for increased volatility in index options meant that larger sized bargains were struck in the FTSE 100 index options than in individual stock options.

In American-style FTSE much of the action by early afternoon was in June 4800 call options where one trader bought 1,350 lots at 14-1/2p and another bought 500 lots at 14p expecting the stock market to push higher.
In European-style FTSE the biggest deal was from a buyer of 2,000 July 4,625 puts at about 86p some of which were subsequently crossed.
By 1217 GMT, the FTSE 100 index was up 38.1 at 4645.6.

Over in stock options, supermarket chain Asda Group stood out owing to a short straddle being traded which consisted of 750 July 120 puts and calls sold at 5p and 3-1/2p each and the deal implies a belief the underlying shares will remain flat.
The stock was up 1/4p to 118-3/4p and the deal will make a maximum of 8-1/2p profit if the shares are 120p at expiry.
Similarly, a short straddle was the main deal in conglomerate BTR in which 250 November 220 puts and calls were sold at 16p each. BTR shares edged 1/2p higher to 217-1/2p.

May options in British Telecommunications expire today and ahead of that event one trader rolled forward a short put position by buying back 300 May 460 puts at 11p and selling 300 November 460 puts at 38p.
The November puts will make money if BT shares are above 460p at expiry. The stock gained 5-1/2p to 450-1/2p.
